title: Software Developer
summary: Coding assistants now write first drafts of functions, tests and documentation, so the value of a developer is moving from typing code to deciding what should be built, reviewing what the AI produced and owning the result in production.
skills: AI-assisted coding workflows and code review
Deep knowledge of one business domain
note: Demand for software roles keeps growing, but entry-level work is the most exposed: juniors who can ship with AI tools stand out.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
summary: Machine learning engineers build and run the AI systems everyone else is adopting. AI tools speed up their pipelines and experiments, but evaluation, reliability and judgment about real-world data remain firmly human jobs.
skills: LLM application patterns (retrieval, agents, tool use)
note: AI and machine learning specialists are among the fastest-growing roles in the World Economic Forum's 2025 outlook.

title: Data Analyst
summary: AI can now clean a spreadsheet, write the SQL and draft the chart. Analysts who thrive use that speed to ask better questions, check the numbers and turn results into decisions people trust.
skills: Statistical reasoning and sanity-checking AI output
Python or SQL with AI copilots
note: Big data and AI skills top the list of fastest-growing skills employers expect to need through 2030.

title: Administrative Assistant
summary: Email triage, scheduling and document preparation are exactly what AI assistants do well, which makes this one of the most exposed roles. The people who stay valuable become operations coordinators who run the tools rather than compete with them.
skills: Advanced use of office AI assistants
note: Administrative and executive assistants are among the roles the WEF expects to decline fastest by 2030.

title: Customer Service Representative
summary: Chatbots now answer the routine questions that used to fill a support shift. Human agents increasingly handle the complex, emotional and high-value cases, and the best ones learn to supervise and improve the bots.
note: Headcount pressure is real, but customer success and escalation roles are growing where companies automate the front line.

title: Bookkeeper
summary: Bank feeds, receipt scanning and AI categorization already automate most transaction entry. Bookkeepers who survive the shift become advisors: they review exceptions, explain cash flow and help owners make decisions.
note: Bookkeeping and payroll clerks are on the WEF's list of fastest-declining roles.

title: Accountant
summary: AI drafts reconciliations, flags anomalies and summarizes tax rules, but clients still pay for judgment, sign-off and advice. Accountants who pair AI speed with advisory skills can serve more clients at higher value.
note: Routine compliance work shrinks while advisory, forensic and controls work holds up.

title: Financial Analyst
summary: Models, data pulls and first-draft reports are fast becoming AI work. The analyst's edge is a sharp point of view, the ability to spot when a number is wrong and the trust to present a recommendation to decision-makers.
skills: Python or advanced Excel with AI
note: Fewer hours go into data wrangling; more go into interpretation and advising.

title: Paralegal
summary: Legal AI tools review documents, summarize case law and draft standard filings in minutes. Paralegals who learn to run and check these tools become more valuable, while purely clerical legal roles shrink.
skills: Verification of AI research and citations
note: Expect fewer pure document-review roles and more legal-operations and legal-tech roles.

title: Lawyer
summary: Research and first drafts are accelerating, but advice, negotiation and courtroom advocacy depend on accountability that AI cannot carry. The practical risk for lawyers is relying on AI output that has not been checked.
skills: Pricing and delivering legal work efficiently
note: Firms are shifting from billable hours on routine drafting toward fixed-fee, higher-judgment work.

title: Graphic Designer
summary: Image generators and AI design suites produce usable assets in seconds, so commodity design work is under real price pressure. Designers who lead with concept, brand systems and taste, and use AI to explore faster, stay in demand.
note: Graphic designers appear on the WEF 2025 list of fast-declining roles, largely because of generative AI.

title: Content Writer and Copywriter
summary: Generic copy is now nearly free to produce, so the market rewards writers with original reporting, strong opinions, subject expertise and the editing skill to turn AI drafts into something people actually want to read.
note: Volume writing work is shrinking; strategy, expertise-led and brand-voice work is holding.

title: Translator and Interpreter
summary: Machine translation now handles most everyday documents well enough, so routine translation volume is moving to post-editing. Specialists in legal, medical, literary and live interpreting work keep the highest-value jobs.
note: Translators are among the most AI-exposed occupations in academic exposure studies.

title: Journalist
summary: AI can summarize, transcribe and draft, but it cannot knock on a door, earn a source's trust or decide what matters. Journalism is being reshaped around original reporting and verification.
note: Newsroom economics remain tough; original reporting is the most AI-resistant part of the job.

title: Video Editor
summary: Automatic transcripts, captions, silence removal and rough cuts take hours out of editing. Editors who control story, pacing and taste, and who use AI to deliver faster, win more work.
note: Demand for video keeps rising, but the time per edit is falling quickly.

title: Marketing Manager
summary: AI multiplies content output and analytics, so marketing managers spend less time producing and more time deciding: positioning, budget, brand and which experiments are worth running.
note: Strategic marketing roles hold up; execution-only roles are consolidating.

title: Social Media Manager
summary: Captions, scheduling and reporting are heavily automated. The durable value is a feel for culture, community management and the judgment to know what a brand should and should not say.
note: One person with AI can now run what used to take a small team.

title: Sales Representative
summary: AI researches prospects, drafts outreach and updates the CRM, which gives salespeople more time for the conversations that close deals. Relationship and negotiation skills become the whole job.
note: Sales and relationship roles stay in demand; inside-sales admin work shrinks.

title: HR Specialist and Recruiter
summary: AI screens resumes, drafts job posts and answers policy questions. The human side of HR, including hiring judgment, fairness, employee relations and culture, becomes the core of the role.
skills: Fair and lawful use of AI in hiring
note: Reskilling programs are creating new work for HR teams that understand AI.

title: Project Manager
summary: Status reports, meeting notes and schedules are increasingly automated. Project managers are judged on what AI cannot do: aligning people, resolving conflict and making trade-offs under uncertainty.
note: AI rollouts themselves are generating demand for people who can manage change.

title: Teacher (Secondary School)
summary: AI helps teachers plan lessons, differentiate material and draft feedback, but teaching is a relationship. The WEF expects secondary teachers to be among the roles with the largest absolute job growth this decade.
skills: Designing assessment in the AI era
note: Secondary teachers appear among the jobs with the largest absolute growth in the WEF's 2025 report.

title: Registered Nurse
summary: Nursing is hands-on, judgment-heavy and human, which makes it one of the safest professions from AI. AI mostly lightens documentation and monitoring so nurses can spend more time with patients.
note: Nursing professionals are on the WEF list of roles with the largest absolute growth.

title: Physician
summary: AI is becoming a second reader for scans, a scribe in the exam room and a research assistant. The diagnosis, the decision and the conversation with the patient remain the physician's responsibility.
note: Aging populations keep demand high; AI mainly reduces paperwork burden.

title: Pharmacist
summary: Automation already counts pills and checks interactions. Pharmacists are moving toward clinical roles: counseling, medication management and prescribing where regulations allow.
note: Retail dispensing is consolidating; clinical pharmacy roles are expanding.

title: Psychologist and Therapist
summary: Therapy depends on a human relationship, so AI exposure is low. AI helps with notes, research and between-session tools, and clinicians who understand AI's risks and benefits are increasingly sought after.
note: Demand for mental health care continues to exceed supply in most countries.

title: Personal Care Aide and Caregiver
summary: Caring for people in their homes is one of the least AI-exposed jobs there is. AI and sensors may help with reminders and reporting, but the work itself is physical, relational and growing fast.
note: Care economy jobs are among the largest sources of new jobs worldwide.

title: Electrician
summary: Skilled trades are among the most AI-resistant careers, and electricians also benefit from the build-out of data centers, EV charging and renewable energy. AI helps mostly with quotes, code lookups and paperwork.
skills: Solar, battery and EV charger installation
Using AI for quotes and code lookups
note: The energy transition and data-center construction are adding demand for electricians.

title: Plumber
summary: Plumbing is hands-on problem-solving in unpredictable spaces, which robots and AI are far from mastering. The upside of AI here is admin: faster quotes, scheduling and customer follow-up.
skills: Heat pumps and efficient water systems
note: Shortages of skilled trades workers are reported in many countries.

title: Construction Worker
summary: Construction workers are among the jobs with the largest absolute growth expected by the WEF. AI touches planning and safety, but the physical work on site remains human.
note: Construction workers appear among roles with the largest absolute growth in the WEF 2025 report.

title: Truck and Delivery Driver
summary: Self-driving trucks and delivery robots get headlines, but large-scale deployment is slow and uneven. For now, e-commerce keeps delivery jobs growing, while AI route planning changes how the work is organized.
note: Delivery drivers appear among the largest absolute job gains in the WEF outlook; autonomy is a longer-term risk.

title: Retail Cashier
summary: Self-checkout and cashierless stores are steadily reducing cashier roles. The good news: retail experience transfers well into customer service, inventory, sales and supervisory jobs.
note: Cashiers and ticket clerks are among the fastest-declining roles in the WEF report.

title: Chef and Cook
summary: Cooking is physical, sensory and fast-paced, so AI exposure is low. AI helps with menu ideas, costing, ordering and food safety records, freeing chefs to focus on food and team.
note: Hospitality demand is cyclical, but cooking itself is not being automated at scale.

title: Real Estate Agent
summary: Listings, market reports and paperwork are increasingly AI-written. Clients still want a trusted human for the biggest purchase of their life, so local knowledge and negotiation remain decisive.
note: Agents who use AI for marketing and admin can serve more clients.

title: Insurance Underwriter
summary: Standard policies are increasingly priced and approved by algorithms. Underwriters remain essential for complex, high-value and unusual risks, and for overseeing the models themselves.
note: Automated underwriting continues to absorb standard personal-lines work.

title: Architect
summary: Generative design and AI rendering speed up concepts and drawings. Architects still own the brief, the client relationship, code compliance and the responsibility for buildings people live in.
note: Sustainable retrofit and green building work is growing.

title: Mechanical Engineer
summary: AI accelerates simulation, design exploration and documentation. Engineers still decide what is safe and buildable, test in the physical world and take professional responsibility for results.
note: Energy, robotics and manufacturing reshoring support demand.

title: Farmworker
summary: The WEF expects farmworkers to see the largest absolute job growth of any role this decade. Precision agriculture adds sensors, drones and AI advice, which creates new skilled roles on the farm.
note: Farmworkers top the WEF list of largest absolute job growth to 2030.

title: Small Business Owner
summary: For small business owners, AI is mostly an opportunity: it can act like a part-time marketer, bookkeeper and assistant. The owners who gain most automate admin and reinvest the time in customers.
note: AI lowers the cost of starting and running a business.
